source: Create a social hangout house with private bedrooms and locked bathrooms where two players can be alone together.

answers.ask: Modern suburban, cosy cabin, something else?
answers.answer: Use a modern suburban social hangout house.

answers.ask: How many bedrooms - two, or a houseful?
answers.answer: Use two private bedrooms to keep the house small and plainly playable.

answers.ask: Can bedroom doors lock as well, or only the bathrooms?
answers.answer: Bedroom doors can lock as well as the bathrooms, so two players can have privacy in either space.

blob:
## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: Modern suburban, cosy cabin, something else? A: Use a modern suburban social hangout house.
- [author] scale — Q: How many bedrooms - two, or a houseful? A: Use two private bedrooms to keep the house small and plainly playable.
- [author] goal — Q: Can bedroom doors lock as well, or only the bathrooms? A: Bedroom doors can lock as well as the bathrooms, so two players can have privacy in either space.
- [agent_inferred] bathroom_count — Q: How many lockable bathrooms should the small two-bedroom house contain? A: Use two bathrooms, one beside each bedroom.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a small modern suburban social hangout house as one fully enclosed interior. Arrange a central shared living room with a short hall leading to exactly two private bedrooms and two bathrooms, one bathroom beside each bedroom. Size every private room for two avatars and give each bedroom and bathroom a visible closable door. Keep common and private circulation clear in one compact floor plan.

## Genre
The genre is Roleplay & Avatar Sim. The house supports open-ended social hanging out rather than a scored, quest, or task loop.

## Shape and preset
Use `interior-single`, because the entire playable map is one compact house interior with no exterior transition. The preset is none; the genre's town, wilderness, pet-care, and runway presets do not describe a single private hangout house.

## Config requirements
Use `social-hub` for the central shared living room. The two bedroom doors and two bathroom doors are direct scene geometry. The shared catalogue has no canonical option for player-controlled privacy locks, so no unrelated gate option is substituted.

## Layout requirements
Place four free-text Gate controls with no canonical option ID: one on each of the two bedroom doors and one on each of the two bathroom doors. Each control is sited at its doorway and makes that room lockable for a pair of occupants.

## Layout components
Build one compact single-floor house interior with a central shared living room, one short connecting hall, two private bedrooms, and two bathrooms, one adjacent to each bedroom. All four private rooms have closable doors and enough clear floor area for two avatars. Exterior walls enclose the map, and the cutaway isometric composition keeps the common room, hall, and all four private rooms legible.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: the modern house composition leads, and its simple room connections do not require a generated plan.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Use small scale, driven by room and doorway legibility. The theme is a modern suburban social hangout house. Use `P0`; the entire map is one non-stacked interior and the privacy controls add no geometry capture modifier.
